description: We are a team of four participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, ClimateShift, explores climate-adaptive farming using NASA data, soil analysis, and crop rotation strategies. We focus on climate research, agriculture, data analysis, and visualization. We welcome collaborators with interests in agronomy, soil science, climate science, and data analytics.
summary:
PalawijaPintar is a web-based decision-support platform that helps farmers in Indramayu, West Java, choose suitable crops after rice harvesting. Farmers often select maize, soybean, or mung bean based on habit rather than seasonal water availability, increasing the risk of crop failure and unnecessary irrigation costs.

To address this challenge, PalawijaPintar analyzes 25 years of NASA POWER climate data (2001–2025), combined with SMAP soil moisture, SoilGrids soil characteristics, and the FAO-56 water balance method. The platform compares normal and dry-year conditions across different planting seasons, then evaluates crop water requirements and estimates irrigation needs.

It provides ranked crop recommendations, water-shortfall estimates, and a rotation simulator to help farmers make more informed decisions. By turning NASA Earth observation data into practical agricultural insights, PalawijaPintar aims to support more water-efficient, climate-adaptive, and sustainable farming.
details:
PalawijaPintar is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers in Indramayu, West Java, select suitable crops after rice harvesting. It focuses on three commodities: maize, soybean, and mung bean.

The platform processes 25 years of daily NASA POWER climate data (2001–2025), covering 9,131 days and six weather parameters. It combines this information with SMAP soil moisture, SoilGrids soil characteristics, and the FAO-56 water balance method to evaluate seasonal water availability and crop requirements.

Users can select planting seasons, compare normal and dry-year conditions, explore crop suitability scores, estimate irrigation requirements, and simulate crop rotation patterns. The model considers different crop growth durations: 100 days for maize, 85 days for soybean, and 60 days for mung bean. It then provides ranked recommendations and estimated water shortages to support better decisions.

The project aims to reduce water-related crop risks, improve irrigation planning, and encourage climate-adaptive farming. Its creative approach is transforming complex NASA Earth observation data into practical, accessible agricultural recommendations. The development process uses NASA POWER, SMAP, SoilGrids, the FAO-56 methodology, web application technology, and Claude AI assistance.

Key factors include rainfall variability, temperature, humidity, solar radiation, soil moisture, soil characteristics, crop water requirements, and seasonal differences.
